lines.text: Victoria's brooch holds a baby tooth.
In September 1847, the royal family stayed in the Scottish Highlands.
lines.say: In September eighteen forty seven, the royal family stayed in the Scottish Highlands.

lines.text: Their eldest child, Princess Victoria, lost her first milk tooth.
Prince Albert pulled the tooth himself.
The tooth was made into a thistle brooch for the Queen.
Albert was a hunter who often had stag teeth set in jewelry.
In 1851, he gave her a holly brooch with two stag teeth.

post.caption: Victoria's brooch holds a baby tooth. In September 1847, the royal family stayed in the Scottish Highlands, where their eldest child, Princess Victoria, lost her first milk tooth. Prince Albert pulled it himself, and the tooth was made into a thistle brooch for the Queen. Albert was a hunter who often had stag teeth set in jewelry. In 1851, he gave her a holly brooch with two stag teeth, made by Garrard. It is engraved Dee, September 11, 1850, from Albert.
